verdict.rationale: Jev's fan-out/parallel-questions pattern lets users batch many questions into a single call (12.2x cheaper, 10x faster) and cookbooks like hierarchical classification and reranking apply this at scale across many items, which supports bulk operations. However, this is batching questions within a context window (bounded by the 64k token/32k state limit), not a documented bulk-job or async batch-processing API for large item counts, and there's no evidence of a dedicated bulk/batch endpoint, job queue, or progress tracking for large-scale item processing. missing for 10: a dedicated bulk-batch API/endpoint or job system for large-scale item processing beyond single-call token limits, independent benchmarks of true bulk throughput at scale, and hands-on community confirmation of bulk operations working reliably.
